title: controlplane-subnet-failover-sentinel-and-route-priority-operator
author: Priya Natarajan
release_notes: Adds a control-plane subnet failover sentinel, conditional route-priority operator, Terraform lease resource, and Helm pre-drain hooks to enable automated AZ failover and safe DNS cutover for private deployments.
description: Context: Customers running Redwood Private across multi-AZ VPCs require deterministic and low-risk control-plane failover when an AZ becomes degraded. This PR introduces a failover sentinel and a route-priority operator that coordinate subnet handoff, ENI lease transfer, conditional peering/route adjustments, and a preflight DNS cutover to minimize downtime and avoid split-brain. Motivation: Previous incidents showed manual subnet reallocation and DNS changes were error-prone and caused long recovery windows. We need an automated but controlled mechanism that integrates with the installer, Terraform modules, and Helm hooks so we can perform staged failovers with canary verification and easy rollback. Summary of changes: 1) New sentinel service (installer/cmd/sentinel) that monitors per-AZ ENI health, control-plane pod readiness, and VPC route table metrics; it evaluates failover conditions and triggers a coordinated plan. 2) Route-priority operator (installer/pkg/network/route_operator) that programs route table priorities and temporary peering routes to move control-plane egress to a standby AZ without tearing down existing endpoints. 3) Terraform module: vpc/subnet-lease.tf introduces a Lease resource for ENI/control-plane IPowner claims, with idempotent apply/rollback semantics and preflight plan output. 4) Helm chart: charts/controlplane/templates/pre-drain-hook.yaml adds a pre-drain hook that quiesces control-plane components and emits a checkpoint event before subnet swap. 5) DNS safety: preflight Route53 change batch dry-run and staged record TTL reduction automation to avoid cache poisoning during cutover. 6) Installer integration: new CLI flags and a dry-run mode for staged cutovers, plus detailed operator annotations for manual override. Rollout plan: start with canary in staging (1 cluster), then opt-in beta for customers with a flag, finally enabled by default after 2 weeks of telemetry. Includes a manual abort and automatic rollback if health checks fail. Testing and CI: unit tests for sentinel heuristics, Terraform plan/unit tests, Helm template tests, and an e2e canary that simulates AZ failure; CI pipeline required two runs (first run e2e failed due to timing assumptions, second run passed after adjusting backoff). Backwards compatibility: designed to be opt-in; existing installs not using the Lease resource remain unchanged until Terraform is applied. Operational docs: adds a runbook for forced cutover and a postmortem checklist to verify DNS propagation and route table state. Security: lease operations are audited, and KMS-encrypted state is used for critical actions.
